prize_parts.citation: for the conception and leadership of the IceCube neutrino observatory and the discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, opening neutrino astronomy
for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, which brought atomic frequency standards to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: IceCube (Halzen) and the optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye). After the full exchange, B022 is the most defensible part on the table: the attribution is clean, the 10^-18 level is reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, and the interpretation is stable. Lindroth and Pearce make a fair case that the lattice clock is a new concept, magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, and not merely a refinement of combs or single-ion clocks. IceCube is the other discovery in the room that is secure on the data and independent of interpretation: a diffuse TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrino flux seen in several channels, with the TXS 0506+056 association as supporting evidence. I would word the citation around the diffuse flux and the opening of neutrino astronomy and leave the Galactic-plane result out as too recent. The two parts are unrelated, but I do not regard that as a defect; the prize has often combined distinct achievements, and this pair uses exactly three names without forcing a thin single theme.
statement.case_against: The weak point is still the single name for B002. A cubic-kilometre detector built by hundreds of people, with AMANDA-era work behind it, is exactly where the conceiver-and-leader argument can fail, and I have no external expert input on that history to lean on. If the committee concludes that Halzen alone cannot carry a prize part, the configuration collapses to B022 alone or B022 with a different partner, and the three-name limit then blocks B028 as a partner (five names). For B022, the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is real and the fundamental-physics reach, constants and dark-matter bounds, is so far limits and not discoveries. B028 is the broadest candidate in the room and I do not dismiss it; my objection is timing and the unsettled origin of the correlated and superconducting states, not the reality of the phenomena.

responses.point: B028 is a clean prediction-then-experiment story, independently reproduced across many moire systems, and the unresolved superconductivity should not by itself decide it.
responses.response: I agree that the phenomena are real and the 2011 prediction against the 2018 observation is exactly the structure the prize handles well, and that a citation limited to flat bands and correlated phases would avoid taking a side on the pairing mechanism. I still hold back on timing. Your own case against lists the Cao team, the Dean and Young groups and the Bistritzer question, and a three-name prize forces choices that the field itself has not yet settled. Because B028 would consume all three names it cannot be paired with anything, so choosing it means giving up the whole prize to a field that is under a decade old. I keep it as my first alternative and could be moved by a convincing answer on credit.

responses.point: IceCube and the lattice clock are two scientifically unrelated, measurement-driven discoveries, and if B002 cannot carry a part then B037 or B028 is the better partner for B022.
responses.response: We reach the same configuration, so let me test the fallback. B037 as a partner needs a principle for crediting detector architects that the committee has not agreed, and Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the conceivers and builders, not the leaders of the 2012 analysis, so I do not think it is a safe fallback this year. B028 as partner is excluded by the three-name limit. That leaves B022 alone as the real fallback if the attribution for B002 does not hold. I agree with you that the Galactic-plane signal should not appear in the citation, and I would add that the diffuse flux, not the individual source identifications, should carry the case.

responses.point: B022 should stand alone as a clean two-name prize, and B002 is doubtful because one name stands for a collaboration-scale discovery.
responses.response: I share your doubt about the single name, and it is the main reason I could be moved. Where I differ is that I think the lattice clock is better as one part of a two-part prize than a whole prize, since its fundamental-physics consequences remain largely prospective and so far give bounds. The pending redefinition of the second supports timing but does not decide it. On your Boulder connection, a documented research stay in Hall's laboratory without collaboration with Katori or Ye seems to me a matter for the record and not a ground for recusal, though the committee should decide that for itself.

responses.point: The lattice clock is a new, complete and mature achievement, but you would not pair it with IceCube without a joint argument from colleagues in astroparticle physics.
responses.response: That joint argument is what I can offer. IceCube meets the same standard as the clock: a discovery stable under independent analyses, with a clear origin in one instrument concept. The two share no theme, which means that the weakness of one part cannot contaminate the other. I accept your point that the pairing depends on the Halzen attribution, and until the AMANDA-to-IceCube history is checked with external experts I treat that as the open condition of my position, not as something already settled.

responses.point: B022 is more technological than conceptual, and B028 deserves preference as a platform for strongly correlated matter.
responses.response: The technological character of the clock is a fair concern, but I think it understates the conceptual step: choosing a magic wavelength so that the lattice leaves the clock transition unperturbed is a physics idea, and it opens a precision regime that did not exist, as Lindroth argues. I agree that B028 opens a controllable arena for correlated matter and that is its real strength. My difference with you is on weighing it now against an interpretation that is still moving, which is why it remains an alternative for me and not my first choice.

uncertainties: Whether Halzen alone can be defended as the decisive credit for IceCube, and how AMANDA-era contributors and collaboration leadership are treated; the committee has not yet heard external experts on this.
Whether the committee will regard IceCube plus the lattice clock as a coherent two-part prize rather than a convenience pairing.
Whether B028 is mature enough given the unsettled origin of its superconductivity; I could change my view if the credit question for Cao and Bistritzer is resolved convincingly.
I rely on general knowledge for the formal roles of credited people and the current significance of individual neutrino source identifications.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My work in string theory, cosmology and black-hole physics, my PhD under David Gross and my Uppsala group have no documented connection to any shortlisted candidate or credited person. I note that, as Secretary, my role is procedural and I claim no private knowledge of the committee's deliberations.
